findings.summary: The retry condition `else if (bp.branch)` also fires when the protection read failed for a reason other than 'no rule' (HTTP 5xx, 401, network error) or the 200 body could not be parsed, so setup could run `init --add branch-protection` against an existing rule. A stricter guard would retry only on 404 / not protected.

findings.summary: The 'never runs a write command' test only inspects `gh api` calls for -X, --method, -f, -F; it misses --input and other gh write subcommands. An allowlist of exact read commands would be stronger.

findings.summary: repairSteps re-runs `init --add branch-protection` whenever the protection GET fails unless classified as HTTP 403; a 5xx or network error while a rule exists could trigger a re-apply over a customised rule. Consider retrying only on a confirmed 404 and reporting anything else as unknown. Not attacker-triggerable.
